assessment: Full assembly plausibly reduces customer insertion work and exposes incompatibilities before dispatch; these benefits remain unmeasured. Repeated three-compartment orders took seven to nine minutes, limiting claims that full assembly inherently prevents the time target. Mixed batches contained every extreme delay, suggesting complexity or switching. Overlapping widths weaken a width-only insertion explanation. Missing-part reports and customer confusion remain separate failure signals. Diagnostic trials cannot establish pilot success.

openings.claim: Order-specific reusable staging trays may reduce mixed-batch selection and checking interruptions enough to retain full assembly.
openings.delta: Changes shared-bin retrieval while preserving assembled delivery; separates selection overhead from insertion difficulty.
openings.prediction: Matched staged orders show lower total labor time and fewer retrieval corrections, with little insertion-time change.
openings.probe: Use 12 spare-board samples as six matched pairs across layouts. Alternate workers and condition order: current selection versus order-specific staging. Separately time staging, selection, insertion, checking, and packing, counting both workers’ labor. Independently verify packed components and color. Reject this explanation if insertion dominates or staging cancels savings.
assumptions: Reusable staging uses existing resources within the initial budget without recurring material additions.
Trials fit available time without delaying delivery.

openings.claim: An order-specific placement diagram may resolve short-partition uncertainty better than the current three-layout diagram.
openings.delta: Targets layout identification while retaining dimensions, compartment counts, exterior color, capacity, and removable partitions.
openings.prediction: With verified complete kits, customers using the order-specific diagram request less short-partition guidance and more often achieve their arrangement.
openings.probe: Randomly assign ten participants to existing or order-specific diagrams, balancing layout difficulty. Record unaided arrangement within ten minutes, short-partition errors, and help requests. Treat results as screening evidence; verify replacement-diagram costs before deployment.
assumptions: The replacement insert stays within both cost caps and the delivery schedule.
Difficulty is partly informational; null results leave physical fit and other causes open.
